description: Role -> tier -> worker. The rules (rules/) speak only of tiers and roles; the concrete model, effort and per-host role priorities are set in the workers list here. Model API support, app modes, launcher policy and measured results are kept distinct. Codex delegates cannot use ultra.
precedence: model-bindings.local.json overrides keys at the same path (dictionaries merge key by key; arrays and scalars are replaced whole; workers_local merges rows by id). harness-route.py selects a worker from the workers list, the role, the host and the declared budget, and the launcher uses that resolved value. Nothing queries usage or servers at start-up. Runtime boundary: docs/runtime-boundary.md.

probed: opus alias (claude -p --model opus: resolves to claude-opus-5-5)
claude-sonnet-5-5 (claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5: OK on Claude Code 2.1.283; the CLI logs unrecognized_model and disables the advisor for it)
catalog.source: Claude Code 2.1.280; IDs not probed come from the claude-api skill model table (cached 2026-06-24)
catalog.note: In-process agents pin effort in frontmatter (opus-architect high, claude-implementer medium), so the alias switch to Opus 5.5 does not change their effort. claude-run.sh passes --effort explicitly. Opus 5.5's API default effort is medium (one below Opus 5's high) — never rely on the default.

openai.effort_note: The Astra API lists low/medium/high/xhigh/max explicitly. Codex app Ultra is an automatic sub-agent mode; the delegation launcher and router refuse it under the no-redelegation contract. max is -b only. The enumeration in the official config-reference is separate and does not replace a measured success on the installed CLI. The human main session's model and mode are never changed.

probe.command: codex exec -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort=low -s read-only "Reply with exactly: OK"

probe.note: A catalog or leaderboard listing is not runnability. A candidate enters alternatives/pending_replacement only with a probe result and date; it becomes a worker row only after a successful probe on the installed CLI and account.

properties: data never leaves the LAN (which does not mean the same machine — security-boundary.md)
local.note: Model, hardware and endpoint live in model-bindings.local.json. vendors.local.endpoint requires base_url and model; wire, max_tokens and max_input_chars are optional. The request timeout is local-run.sh -t seconds (default 300, max 570). Requests happen only through local-run.sh; SessionStart never queries the server. Input format, access limits and failure handling: docs/runtime-boundary.md. Addresses, model names and measured figures stay in local settings only.

orchestrate.switch: User-selected main model stays selected; no automatic host/model switch.
orchestrate.note: The host the human started is the orchestrator. Bindings are recommended tiers and never change an already chosen main model automatically.

second_opinion.when: Consequential uncertainty unresolved by task checks, or project/user-required advice; not every planning folder.
second_opinion.vendor: different from actual design author(s); defaults to host author unless --author-vendor supplied
second_opinion.note: max is -b + --wait only. Codex delegate ultra is refused because it redelegates automatically. Model and app support evidence follows vendors.openai.guidance_sources.
second_opinion.effort_rule: Use the selected host/role binding and launcher-supported effort; no common vendor-independent effort floor.

implement.escalate_when: one step, only when a reasoning shortfall is diagnosed

write.tier_rule: decided by audience and open decisions
write.vendor_rule: decided by writing specialty (specialties); fields without a specialty use the tier default

review.tier_rule: the risk tier is the floor
review.tier1_route: Affected checks + diff; when independent review is needed, review_gate with actual target authors (--author-vendor) selects a different vendor.
review.tier2_route: review_deep (B+) with actual implementer authors; optional separate spec gate uses designer authors. Required pairs must also use different reviewer vendors.
review.tier2_inline_rule: Supply focused inline context or an exact bounded readable file/range. If access is unavailable inline the target or report incomplete; never review unseen material.
review.tier2_vendor_precedence_exception: Choose a vendor different from the author. The reviewer is not pinned to the orchestrating vendor, and when two reviews are required the reviewers must differ from each other too.
review.round_limit_note: Normally one round; second only for a blocker. Confirmation counts; no recurring whole-repo review.

vendor_precedence.rationale: Separating design, implementation and review across a perspective different from the author's comes first; spreading quota is a side benefit. The route is re-selected from the actual authoring vendor, risk and availability.
vendor_precedence.overridden_by: specialties and hard constraints (vision, web, isolation, platform, data that must not leave) beat this order. Never the other way round.
vendor_precedence.note: Implementation, advisory and review candidates are ordered per host through the workers' role priorities: the OpenAI rows form the implementation lane on the Claude host, the Claude rows on the Codex host. The HTML specialty is kept.

budget.rationale: The user's declaration feeds route selection. No automatic usage lookup and no main-model switching.

values.normal: No additional declared budget limit. Does not guarantee the account's actual remaining usage.
values.tight: Keep the order; skip optional work only — second opinions, tier promotions.
values.exhausted:<vendor>: Skip that vendor's slot. Example: exhausted:openai.

budget.note: harness-route.py reads the declaration; a missing or unrecognised value is normal. SessionStart neither queries usage nor injects a BUDGET line. tight/exhausted never justify skipping required verification.

specialties.specialty: writing: design documents / operating manuals / per-language text / commit and release notes
specialties.rationale: no writing score on the leaderboards — spare

policy.rules: Fill a slot from the primary; confirm when the secondary lands in the same band, and when they disagree follow the secondary for long implementations only and record it in the evidence column. Items on neither source are filled from own measurements or experience, with the evidence type marked.
policy.recheck_trigger: Actual model adoption, repeated task failure or observed performance change; reassess only affected bindings/policies.

selection_policy.basis: Benchmarks (capability, cost, latency, source, date) set initial bindings. Preserve measured scores and distinguish unmeasured cells.
selection_policy.objective: Sufficient task capability at efficient total completion cost/time, including handoff, verification and retries.
selection_policy.adjust_when: Repeated real-task mismatch; inspect existing run evidence and use local overrides for project-specific differences.
selection_policy.scope: Selection orders eligible rows by measured cost with a ±cost_tie_pct tie broken by TTFT; no composite index. Bands are index floors except S (model-fixed).
selection_policy.cross_review: Host chooses the orchestrator; actual artifact authors choose eligible implementers/reviewers. Pass all authors using --author-vendor. Reviews require explicit provenance and a fresh worker; different vendors do not guarantee correctness.
